title: Simulation of Non-Markovian Quantum Accelerated Dynamics via Time-Fractional Schrödinger Equation
authors: Dongmei Wei, Junxiang Wang, Hanxiu Xu, Cancan Chen, Jiaying Wu
abstract: The Time-Fractional Schrödinger Equation (TFSE) is an effective tool for simulating the dynamics of non-Markovian quantum systems. The Quantum Speed Limit (QSL) time characterizes the minimum time required for the evolution of a non-Markovian quantum system. In this paper, Wei's TFSE is employed to simulate the non-Markovian quantum accelerated evolution process in the Resonant Dissipative Jaynes-Cummings (RDJC) model. By solving the QSL time of a time-fractional single-qubit open system, the enhancement mechanism of the system evolution speed induced by the non-Markovian memory effects of the environment is revealed. Further studies show that the optimized acceleration of the system evolution can be achieved by jointly regulating the fractional order, coupling strength, and photon number. Comparative analyses indicate that Wei's TFSE can accurately capture the non-Markovian accelerated dynamical features of the system over the entire fractional order range, whereas Naber's TFSE is applicable only within a limited fractional order interval. In addition, the comparisons of the average simulation time for calculating the dynamical trajectory of the excited-state probability demonstrate that Wei's TFSE has a significant simulation advantage in computational efficiency. Therefore, Wei's TFSE is more accurate and efficient for simulating the accelerated dynamics of non-Markovian quantum systems.
summary: The paper investigates how fast an open quantum system can evolve under non-Markovian conditions by calculating the Quantum Speed Limit using time-fractional equations. It rigorously compares two theoretical frameworks, concluding that Wei's Time-Fractional Schrödinger Equation is both more accurate and significantly more computationally efficient than existing methods for modeling these complex dynamics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the simulation of non-Markovian quantum accelerated dynamics and characterizing the Quantum Speed Limit (QSL) time for such open quantum systems.
main_result: Wei's Time-Fractional Schrödinger Equation (TFSE) is shown to be superior to Naber's TFSE because it accurately captures non-Markovian acceleration over all fractional orders and offers significant computational efficiency.
method: The study employs the TFSE framework, comparing two formulations (Wei's Co-FD vs. Naber's Ca-FD) to simulate dynamics in an open quantum system.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on a single-qubit open system modeled by the Resonant Dissipative Jaynes-Cummings (RDJC) model, incorporating non-Markovian memory effects from the environment.
key_observables: Quantum Speed Limit time ($	au_{QSL}$), $	au_{QSL}/	au$ ratio, and the excited-state probability $P_e(	au)$.
important_parameters: Fractional order ($ eta$), coupling strength ($\lambda$), photon number ($n$), and evolution time ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The QSL calculation utilizes a Margolus-Levitin-type bound for a pure initial state.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem by defining QSL in non-Markovian systems. It then compares two TFSE approaches (Wei's vs. Naber's) using the RDJC model to calculate $	au_{QSL}$. The core of the work involves demonstrating Wei's method's superior accuracy across all fractional orders and its computational efficiency.
